scenario.summary: Threat actors exploit unauthenticated vulnerabilities in email infrastructure like Cisco Secure Email Gateway and Zimbra to achieve persistence and lateral movement. The attack chain includes arbitrary file writes to hijack system scripts executed by cron jobs and bypassing identity boundaries via SOAP and GraphQL requests.

meta.rationale: Prioritize internet-facing Zimbra servers and Cisco Secure Email Gateways. Use the scoping query to populate scope_hosts for behavioural queries.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has exploited vulnerabilities in Zimbra, Cisco Secure Email Gateway, or BeyondTrust to achieve remote code execution and persistent access through script overwrites and identity boundary bypasses.

references.name: Metasploit Wrap Up: Breaking Zimbra's Identity Boundaries

blind_spots.risk: Proprietary appliances may not export full URL paths or headers by default, making it difficult to distinguish exploit traffic from legitimate SOAP requests.
blind_spots.question: whether the specific SaveDraftRequest or MRS payload was delivered
blind_spots.requires: detailed HTTP access logs from the appliance exported to hb_http_activity
blind_spots.remediation: Enable and ingest raw appliance access logs into the centralized logging platform.

blind_spots.risk: If auditing is not enabled on the appliance itself, the transient execution of a malicious script may leave no trace in the centralized logs.
blind_spots.question: what code the core_watch.sh script executed before it was potentially reverted
blind_spots.requires: real-time process auditing on the appliance endpoint
blind_spots.remediation: Deploy osquery or a similar auditing agent to all network appliances.

hunt.name: Email Infrastructure Compromise and Impersonation
hunt.description: This hunt identifies mail appliances exposed to recent high-severity vulnerabilities, then looks for evidence of multi-stage exploitation. It starts by analyzing authentication bypass attempts on Zimbra and exploit request paths for Cisco SEG and BeyondTrust. The second phase corroborates this early access with evidence of persistence through the modification of system scripts like core_watch.sh and their subsequent execution via cron. An agent evaluates the full compromise chain to identify compromised gateways for isolation and forensic review.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, request_uri, COUNT(*) AS attempts FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE (LOWER(request_uri) LIKE '%/graphql%' OR LOWER(event_type) LIKE '%soap%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, request_uri HAVING attempts > 20
config.description: Detect rate-limit bypass and credential stuffing on Zimbra Network Edition GraphQL endpoints.
config.expected_signal: High volumes of auth attempts on GraphQL from external IPs indicate a rate-limit bypass attempt.

primitive_config.label: Zimbra GraphQL auth anomalies

config.description: Determine whether to trigger containment based on the agent's verdict.
Immediately prevent lateral movement and further data exfiltration from the compromised mail appliance.
config.instructions: Isolate the appliance from the network. Revoke all active sessions for the appliance service accounts and any administrator credentials used to manage it.

config.description: Conduct manual investigation to determine the impact of email impersonation or data access.
config.instructions: Inspect Zimbra audit logs for unauthorized SaveDraftRequest events to identify which accounts were used for impersonation. Review Cisco SEG logs for TAR/PAX file processing errors that may indicate exploitation attempts.

config.description: Restore the appliance to a known good, patched state and apply hardening measures.
config.instructions: Apply the latest security patches for Zimbra (10.1.17+), Cisco Secure Email Gateway, and BeyondTrust. Restrict access to GraphQL and SOAP endpoints to known internal administrative IP ranges.
